title.rendered: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Dan Jaffe support Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier

When Institute Trustee Alison Poorvu Jaffe learned she had colorectal cancer, the diagnosis was even more of a shock because of her age—she was only 48 years old. Now, many years later, she is equally shocked to learn of the disease’s dramatic rise among people in their 20s and 30s—and is committed to support whatever it takes to curb its trajectory.

Colorectal cancer among young people is expected to increase by 90% by 2030, according to Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, director of the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber. Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, recently renewed their support for the center, one of the first in the country dedicated to younger patients with colorectal cancer, with a $100,000 gift to fund the efforts for prevention, detection, and treatment. Ng’s innovative work examines every angle of the disease—from molecular biochemistry, mutations, and gene expression patterns to diet, lifestyle, and the immune system—to uncover what’s driving the disease and develop novel ways to intercept it sooner.

“Given the number of components that the center addresses, we felt a gift of discretionary funds would allow Dr. Ng to balance and fund the areas that she feels need it most,” said Poorvu Jaffe.

excerpt.rendered: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, renewed their support for the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber to help stem the disease’s dramatic rise among people under 50.

title.rendered: Wheeling in the years: The Pan-Mass Challenge produces origin story video

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography courtesy of the Pan-Mass Challenge

Great things can be inspired by loss, and the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) is among them. As a college student, PMC Founder Billy Starr lost his mother to melanoma. In 1980, the athletic youth channeled his grief into action, cobbling together a two-day, 200-mile biking adventure with 36 people, and raised $10,000 to benefit Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

This year, to mark its 45th ride and to celebrate crossing a phenomenal $1 billion in lifetime fundraising, the PMC created a film bringing its origin story to life. Screened at Dana-Farber and available on its website, the film is a poignant celebration of a grassroots event among friends that blossomed into what is now the most successful athletic fundraiser in the world.

“The initial ride was a group of friends and stragglers and pirates and convoys who, by hook or by crook, were going to get to Provincetown on their bikes in two days,” says journalist Ken Shulman, a volunteer at that 1980 event, and now a 29-year rider himself. The 17-minute video includes early footage of riders interspersed with lessons learned and statistics achieved.

“In 1980, there was no plan for 1981. It was just something I needed to do,” says Starr, who ultimately created not just a philanthropic community, but the bike-a-thon industry, because he wanted to be part of the miracle of curing cancer. “The PMC is in the business of hope.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating PMC Heavy Hitters
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as "Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A special ribbon-cutting ceremony was held in December 2023 to commemorate the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion.

img.alt_text: PMC Director of Stewardship Meredith Beaton Starr and PMC Founder and Executive Director Billy Starr

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge's record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

img.alt_text: Bicycle riders on an unpaved path in the woods

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) celebrated its top 2023 fundraisers at a May 10 event held at Encore Boston Harbor.

Co-presented by the Red Sox Foundation and M&T Bank, the PMC is the largest single donor to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Heavy Hitters are a special group of riders who exceed their fundraising commitment to reach the annually determined benchmark—in 2023, that level was $10,000. A record 90% of all 2023 Heavy Hitters rode the 2024 PMC.

“Heavy Hitters represent 35% of all committed riders, but you represent 65% of the annual gift. Your impact is substantial,” said PMC Founder and Executive Director and Institute Trustee Billy Starr in his opening remarks. “As I’m fond of saying, there’s a lot riding on us.”

excerpt.rendered: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as “Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the PMC’s $1 billion milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber leadership welcomed dedicated members of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community for a special event celebrating their success raising more than $1 billion since 1980 and the transformative impact these funds have had on the lives of our patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved riders contributed $1.2 million to the Pan-Mass Challenge's record-breaking gift of $75 million in 2024.

img.alt_text: Bicycle riders on an unpaved path in the woods

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Unpaved
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride over the scenic backroads of the Berkshires in western Massachusetts that raises funds for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: A group of bicycle riders riding along a wooded path

title.rendered: HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge is open at Dana-Farber

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by John Deputy

An official ribbon-cutting ceremony in May celebrated the establishment of the new HomeGoods Young Adult Lounge, a comfortable space to relax and access resources before and after treatments. This special space for adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients provides a more age-appropriate setting for this unique patient population to build relationships with others in their age group. HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation made a $3.6 million gift to Dana-Farber to create the new lounge, with donations from generous shoppers. The gift also supports the HomeGoods Adolescent and Young Adult Oncology Research Fund, and the Pediatric Patient Assistance Program through HomeGoods Housing Grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Creating community for adolescent and young adult patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day, nearly 50 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients—those between the ages of 15 and 39—come to Dana-Farber for treatment, but many never connect with one another because they wait for appointments on different floors.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods supports families facing cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Donations from HomeGoods and Homesense shoppers at more than 900 locations nationwide funded cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Teen Cancer America Partnership anniversary honored by rock legend Sir Roger Daltrey
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Legendary rock icon Sir Roger Daltrey, lead singer of The Who and co-founder of Teen Cancer America (TCA), visited Dana-Farber Cancer Institute on Aug. 26 to mark the 10th anniversary of Dana-Farber’s partnership with TCA.

img.alt_text: Lindsay Frazier, MD and Sir Roger Daltrey

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Liposarcoma Research Initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift from Haroun Family drives critical research for adult patients with Ewing sarcoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rob Haroun and his wife, Julie, established the Haroun Family Fund with a generous gift of $1 million. Under the leadership of Suzanne George, MD, chief of the Division of Sarcoma, the fund will support innovative research aimed at discovering the next breakthroughs in treating Ewing sarcoma in adults.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sasha Pedro

On May 4, the Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute gathered at the Ritz-Carlton in Boston for a special evening of cocktails, dinner, and a live auction, which raised more than $400,000. The 170 guests in attendance were also treated to a discussion emcee’d by WCVB-TV’s Susan Wornick, with panelists Suzanne Bloomberg, Friends Board of Directors member; Anne Gross, PHD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, senior vice president of Patient Care Services and chief nursing officer at Dana-Farber; and Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the Division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber.

The Friends is a volunteer community that raises funds to support a wide range of research and patient care programs and provides services that enhance Dana-Farber’s healing environment. Since their founding in 1976, the Friends have raised more than $50 million in support of Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

excerpt.rendered: On May 4, the Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute gathered for a special evening that raised more than $400,000. Since 1976, the Friends have raised more than $50 million for Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology…

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Society Dinner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 24, more than 200 guests gathered at the Four Seasons Hotel Boston for the annual Dana-Farber Society Dinner.

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Dana-Farber Society Dinner pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: NYC reception spotlights future of research and care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Trustees, Pan-Mass Challenge Heavy Hitters, supporters, and friends gathered at Cure in New York City to meet Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD, and engage in conversation about the path forward for Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Three people speaking at an event on stage

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rybacki Memorial surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thirty years ago, 16 golfers in the first Rybacki Memorial Golf Tournament raised $1,200 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. In 2022, 150 golfers raised more than $145,000

img.alt_text: Larry and Chris Rybacki pose for a photo while golfing

title.rendered: Celebrating 40th anniversary of Kraft Family Blood Donor Center

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by John Deputy

Whole blood and platelet donors were the stars at Gillette Stadium on April 7 for the annual Kraft Family Blood Donor Center Breakfast of Champions. This year’s event was hosted in Gillette Stadium’s newest event space, the G-P Atrium, and marked the 40th anniversary of the Kraft Center. Institute Trustee Dan Kraft congratulated guests for their outstanding contributions, and Institute President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, thanked donors for the lifesaving difference they made, a message underscored by Ken Anderson, MD, program director for the Jerome Lipper Multiple Myeloma Center at Dana-Farber and the Kraft Family Professor of Medicine. A panel discussion with a longtime Kraft Center donor and a Dana-Farber patient was hosted by WBZ sports reporter Steve Burton, whose father was both a former Patriots player and a patient of Anderson’s.

excerpt.rendered: Whole blood and platelet donors were the stars at Gillette Stadium for the annual Kraft Family Blood Donor Center Breakfast of Champions. This year’s event marked the 40th anniversary of the Kraft Center.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kraft Family Blood Donor Center Breakfast of Champions
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly 300 blood and platelet donors from the Kraft Family Blood Donor Center were invited to Gillette Stadium for the annual Kraft Family Blood Donor Center Breakfast of Champions on April 30.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Trustee Dan Kraft speaking from a podium

jetpack-related-posts.title: Honoring whole blood and platelet donors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kraft Family Blood Donor Center celebrates the compassionate individuals who give so generously at the center’s annual Breakfast of Champions. Sunday, Apr. 6 marked the 41st anniversary of the Kraft Family Blood Donor Center.

img.alt_text: Two people stand with a commemorative Kraft Center Patriots jersey

jetpack-related-posts.title: Krafts champion early detection and prevention for at-risk communities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a gift of $5 million to The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Kraft Family will bring Dana-Farber’s lifesaving early detection and prevention programs to more people at risk of developing cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber’s Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner was held in March, recognizing the most generous donors in the community to the Palm Beach Annual Appeal and The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Phyllis Krock and Laurie H. Glimcher

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bill Pomeroy gives the gift of access to patients with blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After his successful transplant, Pomeroy was inspired to help create better outcomes for patients like him. In 2005, he founded the William G. Pomeroy Foundation® to raise awareness and fund initiatives to improve access to blood cancer care. Pomeroy and his foundation have since made gifts totaling more than $1…

img.alt_text: Bill Pomeroy with William G. Pomeroy Foundation banners

jetpack-related-posts.title: Visionary donors aim to make early detection more comprehensive and accessible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Peggy and Greg Strakosch are visionaries whose recent gift will empower Dana-Farber to take the next step in producing a blood test that can identify patients most at risk for developing a BRCA-related cancers.

title.rendered: First annual Lubin Family Foundation Scholar Award Symposium

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

A first annual symposium on May 8 celebrated the Lubin Family Foundation Scholar Award Program, offering guests an opportunity to hear about advancements in cancer care and research. The 2022 and 2023 Lubin Scholars were introduced by their mentors, highlighting how the enhanced mentorship component of the program continues to support their successes. The afternoon also featured an announcement of the 2024 cohort, and a keynote address by Nobel Laureate Harold Varmus, MD. The foundation established the award program to help support and retain the brightest physician-scientists in academic medicine as they launch their research careers.

excerpt.rendered: The Lubin Family Foundation established the symposium and award program to help support and retain the brightest physician-scientists as they launch their research careers.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier

The Meghan McCarthy Research Fund celebrated a major milestone at Dana-Farber in June, surpassing $1 million in funding to support glioblastoma research. The achievement was particularly bolstered in the past year with contributions from the longstanding Pan-Mass Challenge team The Flying Henrys and the Meghan McCarthy Fashion Show at Tewksbury High School, held since 2009.

Meghan McCarthy was a Tewksbury Memorial High School senior active in basketball, soccer, and track and field, whose fundraising in the Jimmy Fund’s Rally Against Cancer inspired countless others to donate before she passed in 2010. Her incredible journey with glioblastoma led the Lowell Sun to name her one of its Most Fascinating People of 2008.

excerpt.rendered: The Meghan McCarthy Research Fund surpassed $1 million in funding to support glioblastoma research at Dana-Farber in memory of a high school athlete and Jimmy Fund fundraiser who passed away in 2010.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On June 30th, the family of the late Heather McMahon, including her parents, nieces, and nephews, attended a ribbon-cutting ceremony outside the laboratory of Jean Zhao, PhD, which revealed a plaque honoring Heather’s memory.

img.alt_text: Group of people in a Dana-Farber lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ravestock Boston
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ravestock Boston, hosted in October by the William Raveis Charitable Fund, raised nearly $150,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s life-changing mission. Held in memory of Meghan Raveis, the event brought together community and live music to benefit Dana-Farber's cancer research and care, while honoring Meghan’s legacy of service to others.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation has awarded $524,081 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to advance novel immunotherapy approaches to treat glioblastoma.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Justin Night

Nearly 150 members of Dana-Farber’s President’s Circle came together at Fenway Park on May 15 for President’s Circle Appreciation Night, an annual event honoring the supporters who generously make annual gifts. Guests enjoyed a reception with remarks from Lisa Diller, MD, director of the Perini Family Survivors’ Center and the David B. Perini, Jr. Quality of Life Clinic at the Institute. President’s Circle members and guests had a bird’s eye view of the Boston Red Sox taking on the Tampa Bay Rays.

excerpt.rendered: Nearly 150 members of Dana-Farber’s President’s Circle, who make generous annual gifts, were honored at this annual event at Fenway Park featuring a reception, an update from the Institute, and a Red Sox game.

title.rendered: Svanberg family establishes endowed chair with focus on early detection

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Nichole Bernier
Photography by Justin Knight

Supporting early detection oncology research had been a dream of Institute Trustee Louise Svanberg, and that dream was fulfilled with the establishment of the Svanberg Family Chair at Dana-Farber. On May 2, a celebration held at the Harvard Club introduced the chair’s first incumbent, Dipanjan Chowdhury, PhD, chief of the Division of Radiation and Genome Stability in the Department of Radiation Oncology and founder and co-director of The Mellen and Eisenson Family Center for BRCA and Related Genes. Chowdhury’s groundbreaking work advances the understanding of cellular response to DNA damage and the early detection of ovarian cancer.

excerpt.rendered: Dipanjan Chowdhury, PhD, was named the inaugural incumbent of the prestigious Svanberg Family Chair at Dana-Farber, which was endowed to provide perpetual support for research into early detection and prevention of cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Brittany Flaherty
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Dana-Farber Campaign has inspired generous gifts for programs across the Institute, including support that has enabled crucial expansion of our patient navigation program. Navigating a difficult diagnosis, juggling work and family obligations, and shuttling from one treatment to another can quickly become overwhelming for patients with cancer—particularly those in medically underserved communities where supportive resources may be limited. One key to alleviating stress for our patients has been building a strong team of patient navigators.

The concept of patient navigators was first introduced in the early 1970s to address breast cancer disparities in Harlem Hospital in New York City. After the hospital introduced navigators and free or low-cost exams and screenings were provided, the five-year survival rate for its patients increased from 39% to 70%. With donor support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute piloted a new community-facing patient navigation program in 2021 to assist patients with transportation, language services, insurance, nutrition, and other social and economic concerns that may be barriers to care. These crucial navigation services can dramatically improve patient experiences and outcomes, but they are not covered by insurance, making philanthropy vital to the program.

Since then, Campaign support has enabled the Institute to hire 6 new community-facing patient navigators, who are now providing extraordinary care to more than 600 patients in our centers for hematologic malignancies, gastrointestinal, breast, thoracic, gynecologic, and genitourinary cancers. Donor support is moving us closer to our goal of hiring community-facing patient navigators in each of our specialized treatment centers and expanding patient navigation into cancer early detection and survivorship—important steps toward delivering more equitable cancer care.

excerpt.rendered: With donor support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute piloted a new community-facing patient navigation program in 2021 to assist patients with transportation, language services, insurance, nutrition, and other social and economic concerns that may be barriers to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: “Sparking Discoveries Through the Power of Community” was the theme for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium in October 2023

img.alt_text: A photo of two people sitting in chairs

jetpack-related-posts.title: Unrestricted support: A powerful vote of confidence
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign is a catalyst for giving at every level, including through the Defy Cancer Fund, and has inspired tremendous unrestricted support from our generous philanthropic community.

img.alt_text: An image of a scientist looking through a test tube (image has blue overlay)

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

Fall 2024
By Impact Staff

We mourn the untimely passing of Scott Edwards, a science writer whose work graced the pages of Impact for more than 10 years. Scott’s exceptional ability to translate complex science into engaging and compelling research reports and articles made him an invaluable member of the Dana-Farber community. With a particular focus on research in hematologic malignancies such as leukemia, lymphoma, and Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, Scott had a role in some of the largest gifts the Institute has ever received. His kind, can-do, collaborative nature endeared him to all, and he will be sorely missed.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC) attracts runners from across the globe as they take on 26.2 miles in support of innovative basic research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute each year.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 10 years ago, Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and his colleagues were the first scientists to discover that MYD88 mutations, which occur in more than 95% of patients with Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM), rely on the BTK protein to function.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Brittany Flaherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is our ambitious, multibillion-dollar fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

Campaign Impact: Ensuring future success through planned giving

The Dana-Farber Campaign has inspired pivotal planned gifts that will make a true difference for children and adults with cancer. In fact, the Dana-Farber Society—comprised of donors who have made a gift in their will, a beneficiary designation, a life income gift, or other planned gift—recently celebrated reaching its ambitious campaign goal of expanding to 2,000 members. This group, whose goal is to provide a dependable future source of funding to the Institute, has doubled in size during the campaign.

Many planned gifts are made with no set requirements for their use and are not tied to a specific type of cancer. Having access to this flexible funding enables Dana-Farber to advance the most promising opportunities to transform cancer care. Planned gifts made during the campaign have also endowed critical positions and provided funds to build on and expedite progress across cancer science and care—today, tomorrow, and well into the future. 

To learn more about the power of data, visit DefyCancer.org.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One way our supporters accelerate campaign efforts is by including Dana-Farber in their estate plans.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Data science and AI allow us to better match patients to clinical trials, identify disparities in cancer care, and pinpoint the most promising treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has played a critical role in the development of more than half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the past 5 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Join Us
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024

Dear Friends,

September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of our Jimmy Fund event season. Summer is always a special time for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund, when people of all ages engage in fun ways to support our lifesaving mission. Whether it was by indulging in all-you-can-eat ice cream at the Scooper Bowl, striking out cancer with the Boston Red Sox, spending a day on the links, or riding across Massachusetts for the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), our community celebrated the warm summer months in the best way possible: defying cancer. It was a very busy and fun summer!

Thanks to the gifts raised through these events and many others, The Dana-Farber Campaign is inspiring and accelerating progress in key Institute priorities and building an incredible foundation to fulfill Dana-Farber’s vision for the future. For example, over the last seven years of the campaign, donor generosity has enabled the establishment of 24 new endowed positions for senior members of the Dana-Farber faculty and 16 new endowed fellowships. This is just one of the countless ways the campaign has enabled further progress at the Institute.

We are grateful to everyone who has joined this important initiative to help us accomplish our goals—with special thanks to the members of The Dana-Farber Campaign Cabinet, and the extraordinary leadership and dedication exemplified by our President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, and Dana-Farber Trustees Michael Eisenson and Monica Chandra, chair and vice chair, respectively, of The Dana-Farber Campaign. In the pages that follow we highlight many stories that demonstrate the inspiring advancements that are supported by so many individuals, organizations, and our special partners like the PMC, Red Sox, and B.A.A.  

There is tremendous momentum within our donor community, and I am confident that we will continue to revolutionize cancer care together with your support and dedication. Thank you for your partnership and for your magnificent generosity.

Sincerely,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

With a grant of $100,000 from the American Brain Tumor Association, Jun Nishida, PhD, is studying the drivers of brain metastases in breast cancer. By researching how varying nutrient levels in different parts of the brain select cancer cells, the team hopes to identify new therapeutic targets in order to improve treatment options for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF accelerates research to better treat pediatric brain tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1991, Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation (PBTF) has helped patients and families cope with a brain cancer diagnosis, offering financial, logistical, and emotional support.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Team Jack Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Team Jack Foundation has donated $400,000 to Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, for her research on pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs). Her project aims to uncover interactions between tumor drivers and brain development, potentially leading to innovative treatments. This collaboration promises new insights into pLGG growth and therapeutic strategies for affected…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Couple commits $2 million to fund groundbreaking clinical trials
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2017, a mammogram revealed that Langley Perer had ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), the very earliest, and highly treatable, stage of breast cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

The American-Italian Cancer Foundation, a collaboration between the U.S. and Italy, has awarded $160,000 to support four Dana-Farber researchers working on a range of projects in triple-negative breast cancer, translocation renal cell carcinoma, multiple myeloma, and melanoma—all of which aim to inform and refine treatment strategies for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating advanced and aggressive kidney cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kidney Cancer Association (KCA) has made $650,000 in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers who are unlocking the molecular mechanisms of a disease that will be diagnosed in nearly 82,000 U.S. residents this year and claim the lives of more than 14,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such…

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

By Michael Quinn
Photography by John Deputy

Special thanks to our friends at Arbella Insurance Foundation, which is making a $50 contribution for each strikeout thrown by a Boston Red Sox pitcher up to $100,000 in total. This promotion has raised more than $1.1 million since 2014 while amplifying Arbella Insurance’s impact as a longstanding Dana-Farber supporter and presenting sponsor of the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Celebrating its 10th anniversary, the Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its Strike Out Cancer program, where $50 per Red Sox strikeout, up to $100,000, is donated each season. With their $100,000 contribution in 2024, the foundation surpassed $1.2 million raised to date, underscoring Arbella Insurance’s vital partnership in defying cancer.

img.alt_text: Check presentation at the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through its Strike Out Cancer Program. At the 2025 WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the team presented a check for $100,000, part of the more than $1.7 million the Arbella Insurance Foundation has contributed to date.

img.alt_text: Arbella Insurance Foundation employees with a check at the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

img.alt_text: A participant in the Jimmy Fund Radio Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

By Michael Quinn

Longtime Dana-Farber donors Sherry and Gerry Cohen made a generous gift of $100,000 to increase community support through our Summer Matching Challenge. jetpack-related-posts.title: Sherry and Gerry Cohen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Esteemed supporters Sherry and Gerry Cohen made a generous gift of $100,000, allowing community gifts to be triple matched throughout our Winter Matching Challenge. This philanthropic leadership resulted in raising $574,998, which will significantly increase our capacity to advance critical research and patient care initiatives.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Science has long been the catalyst for transformative cancer care. More recently, we’ve witnessed revolutionary advances that have benefited patients and those who hold them dear.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber’s Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner was held in March, recognizing the most generous donors in the community to the Palm Beach Annual Appeal and The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Phyllis Krock and Laurie H. Glimcher

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cheryl Kimmens Franke honors husband by supporting cholangiocarcinoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber’s community of supporters is always inspiring, and their meaningful stories moved Cheryl Kimmens Franke to join them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

With a grant of $150,000, Curing Kids Cancer is funding a study into a new combination therapy for treating a form of childhood leukemia caused by a mutation in the KMT2A gene. Previous research at Dana-Farber identified a protein that drives growth of this specific type of leukemia, and researchers are now testing the efficacy of a protein inhibitor in treating it.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CURE Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: CURE Childhood Cancer awarded $330,000 to support research led by Yana Pikman, MD, as she tests a new combination therapy for leukemia with RAS signaling pathway mutations. This new therapy could provide a better, more durable treatment option for pediatric patients, especially those with relapsed leukemia who have developed resistance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wipe Out Kids’ Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a total contribution of more than $230,000, Wipe Out Kids’ Cancer is supporting two Dana-Farber researchers as they work to enhance treatment options for children with leukemia. One study aims to improve the recovery process for stem cell transplant patients, while the other is testing a new combination therapy…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cure Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. The grant also helps launch her career as an…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation targets childhood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2000, a 4-year-old girl named Alexandra “Alex” Scott set up a lemonade stand to raise money for research into childhood cancers like hers.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato made a gift of $100,000 to support research within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia at Dana-Farber. The center is the largest in the world dedicated to the study of Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a slow-growing type of blood cancer that most often forms in the bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fred and Michele Brettschneider
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Cummins
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ellice and David Vittor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards over $1.1 million to Dana-Farber for WM research advancements
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has taken a significant step forward in combating Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM) by awarding four Dana-Farber scientists more than $1.1 million in grants. This generous funding is intended to fuel groundbreaking studies that aim to uncover the mechanisms behind WM development, pinpoint vulnerabilities, and identify…

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards $1.4 million to Dana-Farber investigators, fueling Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than two decades, the International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has been a vital philanthropic partner to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, accelerating research into Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM), a rare, slow-growing blood cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Kayla Carcone
Photography by Michael Blanchard

With gifts totaling $115,000, Stephanie and Austin Dobson established a family fund in support of Lynch syndrome research led by Sapna Syngal, MD, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD. This fund has already garnered meaningful support from Stephanie’s parents, Paul and Bettina Henderson, as well as generous contributions from supporters of Austin’s recent marathon run.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Whittaker Family Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Stephani Batchelor and Andrew Robert Whittaker made an additional gift of $225,000 to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center. This gift supports the leadership of Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF, and their team in diagnosing Lynch syndrome and advancing screenings, treatments, and prevention strategies to help patients…

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mary and John Fowler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Mary and John Fowler’s initial gift establishes the John and Mary Fowler Fund for Lynch Syndrome Research, under the direction of principal investigator Matthew B. Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF. The gift will strengthen the Lynch Syndrome Center’s registry and biobank and accelerate research that will help identify personalized screening, treatment,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rasmussen Family funds research into underlying causes of colorectal cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Anna and Neil Rasmussen are no strangers to medical research in the quest to find answers to chronic illness—one of their children had been living with ulcerative colitis since she was seven years old.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hooley gift to Lynch Syndrome Center boosts prevention and intervention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Linda and Jay Hooley of Hingham, Mass., want to change that. They made a $1 million gift to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center.

img.alt_text: A couple pose for a photo in front of water

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stanley and Carol Riemer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Carol and Stanley Riemer’s most recent commitment has established the Riemer Family Fund for Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection at Dana-Farber, in honor of late relatives who developed pancreatic cancer. Under the leadership of Matthew Yurgelun, MD, their support aims to develop groundbreaking early detection blood tests for high-risk patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sweet family endows first-ever fellowship in Lynch syndrome
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gifts to Dana-Farber, David and JoEllen Sweet hope to alleviate the burden of Lynch syndrome for future generations.

img.alt_text: Two people pose for a photo with a stone sculpture

title.rendered: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ed and Mary Ann Swanson
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ed and Mary Ann Swanson made a gift of $100,000 to support stem cell transplantation research under the direction of Mahasweta Gooptu, MD, including efforts to prevent relapse following transplantation for some patients with acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lindsley named Edward P. Evans Investigator
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Coleman Lindsley, MD, PhD, was recognized as the Edward P. Evans Investigator in MDS research at Dana-Farber at an event in 2023.

img.alt_text: Coleman Lindsley and Michael D. Lewis pose for a photo with a framed lab coat at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to continue advancing pioneering studies into new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Polly and Ming Tsai
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Polly and Ming Tsai made a generous new commitment to advance research by David Barbie, MD, and the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology designed to increase the durability, precision, and effectiveness of lung cancer treatments, like the promising CAR T-cell therapy already in development with previous support from the Tsais.

img.alt_text: Chef Ming Tsai and his wife Polly pose for a photo outside in winter

jetpack-related-posts.title: Li Xu
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Li Xu, MD, MS, MBA, made a $100,000 gift in memory of her parents, Drs. Zhen-Quan Xu and Lin Yuan (pictured), to support pioneering lung cancer research under the direction of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole L. and Philip M. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology and of…

img.alt_text: Two people sitting on a bench in front of some trees

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein made a generous gift in support of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dr. Gerald and Mrs. Mary McGillicuddy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dr. Gerald and Mrs. Mary McGillicuddy made a $100,000 gift to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, a researcher in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. With this gift, Rotow and her team will work to develop better, more effective targeted and immunotherapy options for patients with…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

img.alt_text: Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund logo

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Louis B. Mayer Foundation awarded grants totaling $100,000 to support Dana-Farber’s efforts in developing personalized vaccines to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia; deepening our understanding of neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) to inform better treatment options; and developing personalized treatments for patients at high risk for HER2-positive breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crowley gift accelerates innovative research in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley are longtime supporters of Dana-Farber who made their first gift nearly two decades ago to advance melanoma research in memory of Brian’s sister.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: The promise of personalized cancer vaccines
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised through The Dana-Farber campaign are expanding the benefits of personalized cancer vaccines pioneered here.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

The MPN Research Foundation recently awarded $200,000 to support Sahand Hormoz, PhD, and his research in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN), a category of blood cancers driven by mutations in stem cells. With this funding, Hormoz aims to uncover the mechanisms behind these mutations in the hopes of laying the groundwork for better, more durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants spur cutting-edge MDS research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2019, Dana-Farber established the Edward P. Evans Center for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) with generous funding from the Edward P. Evans Foundation. The foundation recently awarded new grants totaling $1.35 million to three Dana-Farber scientists for novel investigations into MDS, a group of blood disorders caused by abnormal bone marrow…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Michael Quinn

Dana-Farber thanks everyone who supported Rally Against Cancer and Strike Out Cancer with the Jimmy Fund in 2024. With leading contributions from Dell and Fisher Elementary School, Rally teams raised more than $230,000—totaling $7 million since 2007—while Strike Out generated $35,444, with DraftKings matching each donation, up to $25,000 in total.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Strike Out Cancer with the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As the Red Sox returned to Fenway Park this spring, the Jimmy Fund community came together to cheer them on and support Dana-Farber patients. Rally Against CancerSM teams celebrated Opening Day on March 30 and more than 100 fans signed up to strike out cancer by donating for every Red…

img.alt_text: Boston Red Sox and The Jimmy Fund

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Against CancerTM
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Opening Day at Fenway Park, Red Sox and Jimmy Fund fans celebrated by forming Rally Against CancerTM teams in their workplaces, schools, and communities, and raised $270,000 to defy cancer. Fisher Elementary of Walpole, Mass., and Northwestern Mutual Boston were the top fundraisers in a field of 52 Rally…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meghan McCarthy Fund marks milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Meghan McCarthy Research Fund surpassed $1 million in funding to support glioblastoma research at Dana-Farber in memory of a high school athlete and Jimmy Fund fundraiser who passed away in 2010.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September 2025, dreams became reality as more than 200 participants, including Dana-Farber patients, had the once-in-a lifetime chance to play ball at Fenway Park. Thanks to generous support from sponsors, the Boston Red Sox, fundraising teams, and donors, Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised more than…

img.alt_text: Three people at Fenway Park wearing Jimmy Fund jerseys

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

By Kayla Carcone

This generous gift builds on the longstanding partnership with R.J. Corman and the Corman family, which stretches back more than 20 years and began with the company’s founder, the late Richard J. Corman.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift honors late wife and supports multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kenneth Nirenstein remembers his late wife, Harriet, as wise, elegant, and graceful. After Harriet’s passing, seeking a way to keep her memory alive while also making a difference to others, Kenneth made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Harriet Shapiro Nirenstein Fund for Multiple Myeloma Research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of an ocean

jetpack-related-posts.title: Smith Family support inspires others to help speed multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Paul Richardson has found an important partner in Robert and Dana Smith, who recently made a $3 million gift to continue supporting his advanced MM clinical trials research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Changing the trajectory of multiple myeloma and access to care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Joan Suzanne Tomsich was just 48 years old, she thought her life was over. A diagnosis of multiple myeloma led her to thoughts like, “Will I be around to see my kids graduate or witness them getting married?”

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation sustains momentum in multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Multiple myeloma treatments have significantly improved over the past two decades, thanks in part to the driving engine of transformational philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A new $1 million gift from Rev. Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma…

By Kayla Carcone
Photography by Josh Campbell

A gift of more than $100,000 was given to Dana-Farber on behalf of the Estate of Sally Eyring. Her legacy contribution serves to expand critical studies of pancreatic cancer led by Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO. With this contribution, and in honor of Eyring, Meyerhardt aims to refine treatment options and improve methods of diagnosis.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Hallie and John Dovich generously gifted $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, establishing the John and Hallie Dovich Fund. Under the direction of Vincent Ho, MD, this fund will support stem cell transplantation research, to improve transplant outcomes for patients with for patients with myelofibrosis and other blood cancers, ultimately enhancing…

jetpack-related-posts.title: 20 Years of Survivorship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2022, Andrea McGrath celebrated 20 years since her successful stem cell transplant at Dana-Farber. She hosted a survivorship event, raising over $16,000 to benefit the work of her doctor and now friend, Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC, whose advances in stem cell transplantation are continuing to improve outcomes for…

img.alt_text: Andrea McGrath and Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Marrow Donor Program
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The NMDP provided a $400,000 grant to support the research of Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This funding will support her work to improve allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation by identifying genetic factors influencing graft-versus-host disease, potentially leading to more personalized treatment strategies and improved patient outcomes.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Longtime supporter Tina’s Wish recently awarded more than $450,000 over a two-year period to support two Dana-Farber studies into early detection for ovarian cancer—one investigating a new class of microRNA and key biomarkers and how they could be used to develop a personalized blood test, and another examining how epigenetic alterations of fallopian tube epithelial cells could be targeted to treat and detect high-grade serous ovarian cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ovarian cancer is often difficult to treat at later stages and difficult to detect at earlier stages. With a $100,000 grant, the Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance is supporting research at Dana-Farber into the development of an ultrasensitive blood test to detect ovarian cancer at its earliest, and most treatable, stages.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer harnesses power of community to drive cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly 20 years ago, Concord-Carlisle High School hosted its first Kicks for Cancer soccer match to honor the memory of Lois Wells, the mother of assistant men’s soccer coach Steve Wells, who passed away from ovarian cancer. Today, Kicks for Cancer has grown into a vibrant week-long celebration that unites…

img.alt_text: Soccer players mid-game on the field

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Gray Foundation empowers team science against BRCA-mutated cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Philanthropy has transformative power to address society’s intractable challenges. The Gray Foundation is committed to this goal and, with two grants totaling nearly $6 million, is harnessing this power for good through The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Visionary donors aim to make early detection more comprehensive and accessible
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Peggy and Greg Strakosch are visionaries whose recent gift will empower Dana-Farber to take the next step in producing a blood test that can identify patients most at risk for developing a BRCA-related cancers.

content.rendered:
Fall 2024
By Kayla Carcone

In addition to generous donations during his lifetime, two-time cancer survivor William C. Street, MD, left a gift of $327,000 offering vital unrestricted funding for diverse initiatives across the Institute. This gift, and flexible gifts like this one, help to strengthen a spectrum of scientific, clinical, and patient-based activities, from pioneering research to the enrichment of comprehensive care services.
