title.rendered: Celebrating the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

A special ribbon-cutting ceremony was held in December 2023 to commemorate the Pan-Mass Challenge Dining Pavilion. The space—which officially opened when Dana-Farber Cancer Institute – Chestnut Hill launched in 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic—provides a comfortable, full-service eatery where patients and families can rest and recharge during visits. It was named in recognition of the PMC’s long-standing partnership with Dana-Farber as its single largest contributor, with 100% of every rider-raised dollar going to support cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating PMC Heavy Hitters
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the run-up to the 2024 Pan-Mass Challenge on Aug. 3-4, the PMC celebrated top fundraisers from the 2023 ride, known as "Heavy Hitters,” who raise 65% of the PMC’s annual gift.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wheeling in the years: The Pan-Mass Challenge produces origin story video
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, to mark its 45th ride and to celebrate crossing a phenomenal $1 billion in lifetime fundraising, the PMC created a film bringing its origin story to life.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge is moving to Worcester
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), which has raised $1.125 billion for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute since 1980, is relocating its starting line and hub site from Sturbridge to Worcester.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

title.rendered: SoulMates bequest supports breast cancer patients in perpetuity

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Stephanie Lowitt
Photography by John Deputy

When Dana-Farber Trustee Judie Schlager was first diagnosed with breast cancer in 1991, she wished she knew someone who had gone through the same thing, someone to lean on for advice and comfort. “I was home with my thoughts and fears and no one to help me understand on a personal level what I was facing,” Judie remembers. That’s why, in 2012, Judie and her husband, Larry, established SoulMates, the Dana-Farber program that matches breast cancer patients with volunteer mentors who have had a similar diagnosis.

Since then, Judie and Larry, who are both Dana-Farber Society members (donors who have left a charitable gift to Dana-Farber in their estate plans), have made several generous gifts to grow the program and have inspired their family and friends to do the same. They most recently endowed it with a $500,000 bequest commitment.

“My dream is that everyone diagnosed with any form of cancer can have a SoulMate when they need one.”

Judie Schlager

In addition to mentors, participants can join monthly support calls and learn about nutrition, physical therapy, exercise physiology, sleep, acupuncture, expressive arts, and more.

Judie is proud of the impact SoulMates has made on the lives of so many patients. “I think we are put on this earth to leave something good behind. Thirty years ago, I read that the best thing you can lend a friend is a sympathetic ear. My dream is that everyone diagnosed with any form of cancer can have a SoulMate when they need one.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Appeal again surpasses its goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Year after year, the Palm Beach community demonstrates their unwavering commitment to Dana-Farber in many ways including through the Palm Beach Annual Appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: $1 million gift fuels survivorship and precision prostate cancer research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As a child, Donald M. Ephraim, when asked what he wanted to be when he grew up, replied “a philanthropist.” The questioner was impressed with the nobility of the answer.

img.alt_text: Terri Sriberg and Donald M. Ephraim

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS surpasses $4 million milestone in 2024 to advance breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, OOFOS has supported breast cancer research at Dana-Farber through its Project Pink initiative.

title.rendered: Cheryl Kimmens Franke honors husband by supporting cholangiocarcinoma research

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Michael Quinn

Dana-Farber’s community of supporters is always inspiring, and their meaningful stories moved Cheryl Kimmens Franke to join them. After reading about generous donors to the Institute in Impact magazine, Cheryl was encouraged to give as well—and add her own chapter to Dana-Farber’s hopeful story.

Recently, Cheryl made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Arthur J. Franke Fund for Cholangiocarcinoma Early Detection at Dana-Farber. Her generous gift honors the memory of her husband, Art, who was treated at the Institute, and supports a novel screening initiative led by his doctor, Thomas Abrams, MD. Fueled by Cheryl’s and Arthur’s philanthropy, Abrams is working to introduce an alert into medical record software that prompts providers to order additional tests for individuals at risk for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma. His aim is to bring the new tool to primary care offices throughout Boston, alleviating health disparities and improving patient outcomes by providing optimal access to this potentially lifesaving screening intervention.

Grateful for Abrams’ compassionate care, Cheryl hopes her gift accelerates his groundbreaking research to benefit other patients. And she knows this is something her husband would want, too. “Art appreciated everything Dr. Abrams and his team did for him,” she said. “It is a privilege to honor Art by supporting this work.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: September has arrived, and with it the end of summer and the close of another successful Jimmy Fund event season.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

jetpack-related-posts.title: From the Chief Philanthropy Officer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As the year unfolds and progress accelerates, I am grateful for the passion and generosity of our donor community. Together, we have built tremendous momentum and are transforming cancer research and care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defy cancer celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

img.alt_text: People at Fenway Park during the Defy Cancer celebration event

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Because of your support for The Dana-Farber Campaign, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Levy gift supports Dana-Farber’s vision for the future of cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Sarah Salter Levy and Steven Levy learned of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s plans to build New England’s first inpatient hospital dedicated to adults with cancer, they wanted to be among the first to step forward with philanthropic support.

img.alt_text: Sarah Salter Levy and Steven Levy

title.rendered: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Shannon Watterson
Photography by John Deputy

A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.” With additional support through their foundation, Arbella—the Official Auto Insurance Partner of Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund—helps raise funds year-round through several initiatives, including a discount program for Massachusetts drivers and through their annual “Pink Day,” which raises both funds and awareness for cancer screening and prevention.

Arbella’s commitment to striking out cancer is present throughout the year, most notably as the presenting sponsor of the WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, and as a sponsor of the Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by Herb Chambers, Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings, and Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun. The Arbella Insurance Foundation also generously donates $50 for each strikeout a Red Sox pitcher throws each season, up to $100,000.

Thanks to Arbella, the Jimmy Fund community also regularly enjoys a look behind the scenes at Dana-Farber, through the popular “Unsung Heroes of Dana-Farber” social media campaign, showing staff such as janitors, research coordinators, and others who play a “Most Valuable Player” role in support of Dana-Farber’s mission.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through its Strike Out Cancer Program. At the 2025 WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon, the team presented a check for $100,000, part of the more than $1.7 million the Arbella Insurance Foundation has contributed to date.

img.alt_text: Arbella Insurance Foundation employees with a check at the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Special thanks to our friends at Arbella Insurance Foundation, which is making a $50 contribution for each strikeout thrown by a Boston Red Sox pitcher up to $100,000 in total. This promotion has raised more than $1.1 million since 2014 while amplifying Arbella Insurance’s impact as a longstanding Dana-Farber supporter…

jetpack-related-posts.title: WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon surpasses $70 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to thousands of generous supporters from across the country, the 21st annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance raised more than $4 million.

img.alt_text: A participant in the Jimmy Fund Radio Telethon

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella Insurance Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Celebrating its 10th anniversary, the Arbella Insurance Foundation continued its Strike Out Cancer program, where $50 per Red Sox strikeout, up to $100,000, is donated each season. With their $100,000 contribution in 2024, the foundation surpassed $1.2 million raised to date, underscoring Arbella Insurance’s vital partnership in defying cancer.

img.alt_text: Check presentation at the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by 13Photo

The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The annual indoor spin event offered sweeping views of the historic ballpark as riders cycled their way through one to five 45-minute sessions led by Boston-area spin instructors.

This year, riders raised an amazing $750,000, kicking off the 2024 fundraising season for the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) with incredible momentum.

As the PMC, co-presented by the Red Sox Foundation and M&T Bank, cycles closer by the mile toward $1 billion in lifetime fundraising, PMC Winter Cycle is a vital spoke in the wheel for Dana-Farber’s largest annual contributor.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Feb. 4, hundreds of riders assembled at Fenway Park’s 521 Overlook venue for the PMC Winter Cycle.

img.alt_text: Cyclists on stationary bikes at the 2023 PMC Winter Cycle

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Bikers on stationary bikes at the PMC Winter Cycle event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Capehart Photography

Dana-Farber’s Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner was held in March, recognizing the most generous donors in the community to the Palm Beach Annual Appeal and The Dana-Farber Campaign.

Hosted by Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock, the event highlighted the advancements in cancer care and research made possible by this special donor community, which has raised more than $95 million during The Dana-Farber Campaign. Guests also received an update on the Institute’s vision for the future of cancer medicine, with remarks from President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, and Craig Bunnell, MD, MPH, MBA, Morse Family Chief Medical Officer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.title: Over $1 million raised from 2023 Palm Beach Annual Appeal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, the Palm Beach community generously comes together to raise funds for Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Phyllis and Richard Krock at the Palm Beach Annual Appeal

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Appeal again surpasses its goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Year after year, the Palm Beach community demonstrates their unwavering commitment to Dana-Farber in many ways including through the Palm Beach Annual Appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology…

img.alt_text: Attendees of the Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

DefinitiveCares Charity Golf Tournament recently reached an incredible $1 million in total fundraising since its inaugural tournament in 2016. All proceeds go directly to Dana-Farber in support of lifesaving research and patient care.

The tournament began when company founder, CEO, and executive chairman Jason Krantz, along with members of their sales team, raised just over $13,000. Today, the event draws more than 250 people, and its fundraising has consistently surpassed $250,000 for the past three years. And it’s all thanks to the committee of dedicated employees (pictured) who plan the event and have made the tournament a true success year after year.

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Golf supporter receives special award

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

Longtime program sponsor and tournament organizer Michael Aizenstadt (pictured, left) received Jimmy Fund Golf’s 2023 Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award from Suzanne Fountain, vice president of the Jimmy Fund, in recognition of over 35 years of dedication to the golf program.

Aizenstadt has been an integral part of the Jimmy Fund Golf community since the program’s beginning, as a staunch advocate and fundraiser throughout the years. Since 1996, the Ken Coleman Extra Mile Award has been presented to outstanding and longstanding Jimmy Fund Golf volunteers who go above and beyond with their time and energy to support Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf celebrates 40 years of defying cancer from the fairways
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun returned in full force in 2022, with courses around New England and across the country welcoming golfers in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s lifesaving mission.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the earliest days of the Jimmy Fund, passionate and committed individuals have devoted their time, talents, resources, and relationships to raising money in support of a powerful possibility: curing cancer for everyone.

title.rendered: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2023 Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond. This includes Zach Galvin and his team Zach’s Pack (pictured), who received a Lifetime Achievement Award for surpassing $1 million in fundraising as a team. Galvin (pictured center in yellow hat) also received an award for surpassing an incredible $500,000 raised as an individual.

Also honored at the ceremony were First-Time Walker of the Year Kathleen Dunn; First-Time Team Captain of the Year Alynne Johnson; Alumni Walker of the Year Colleen Sullivan; Alumni Team Captain of the Year Mark Leahy; Volunteer of the Year Middleboro High School; and Extra Mile Award winner Amy Killeen. Lifetime Achievement Awards were also presented to Arnold Kraft and David Thau for both surpassing $250,000 in fundraising, and Team Lung Cancer for surpassing $500,000. Top Dana-Farber Employee Teams and Top Corporate Teams were also recognized for their outstanding accomplishments in 2023.

title.rendered: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). In just five days after her diagnosis, Suzanne packed up her family’s entire life in Switzerland and moved back to the Boston area. She knew she needed Dana-Farber.

While incredible strides have been made in the battle against other types of breast cancer, TNBC remains an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis. Suzanne passed away in September 2020—just a few weeks shy of her 44th birthday.

To honor Suzanne’s memory, her family began raising funds to establish a permanent endowment in TNBC research under the direction of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, chief of the Division of Breast Oncology within the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers at Dana-Farber. To date, the fund has raised $630,000, with more than 300 donors contributing. And that number only continues to grow—a testament to the impact Suzanne had on people’s lives.

“Suzanne herself understood the fundamental power of research.”

Meghan Sherwood

“Suzanne herself understood the fundamental power of research,” said Suzanne’s sister Meghan. “We created this fund because we recognized that triple-negative breast cancer is a space where basic research is desperately needed to develop durable treatment options that give young women like Suzanne more time. We are incredibly grateful that our donors come back year after year to make this endowment possible.”

In triple-negative breast cancer, the cancer cells do not have estrogen, progesterone, or HER2 receptors. These three molecules are effective drug targets for other forms of breast cancer, but because they do not exist in TNBC, developing targeted treatments for this disease is challenging. That’s something Suzanne’s loved ones hope to change with the endowment.

“Dana-Farber’s focus on basic research, especially for diseases like triple-negative breast cancer, is going to make a difference,” said Suzanne’s husband Andrew, whose background in biopharma helped inform the decision to seek treatment—and fund research—at Dana-Farber. “When you get that combination of access to clinical trials and basic science understanding, you get the best insights. I’m hoping this fund will enable researchers to think differently about TNBC and try new approaches.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bill and Mary Michels
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bill and Mary Michels gave $170,000 in support of the Suzanne Michels Obenshain Fund for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Research at Dana-Farber. The couple made this generous donation in honor of their daughter Suzanne, who passed away from the disease in 2020.

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Husband honors late wife with gift to support older breast cancer patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the last essay she would write for her college reunion book, Virginia Aisner quoted one of her favorite lines from Vergil’s Aeneid: “Perhaps, at some time, we shall be glad to remember even these things.”

img.alt_text: A closeup shot of Virginia Aisner

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor, a non-profit organization that funds important research for stage IV metastatic breast cancer (MBC), has awarded research grants totaling $700,000 to three Dana-Farber faculty members

jetpack-related-posts.title: OOFOS steps up for breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2023, active recovery footwear brand OOFOS donated $626,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Project Pink initiative, a special program that supports breast cancer research by donating a percentage of online sales to the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: SoulMates bequest supports breast cancer patients in perpetuity
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dana-Farber Trustee Judie Schlager was first diagnosed with breast cancer in 1991, she wished she knew someone who had gone through the same thing, someone to lean on for advice and comfort.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Inspiring hope: Catherine’s journey and the impact of Giving Day
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s annual Giving Day, held on Wednesday, May 21 this year, united patients, families, employees, and supporters worldwide in giving to Dana-Farber's mission to defy cancer.

title.rendered: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation targets childhood cancers

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Kathy Clute

In 2000, a four-year-old girl named Alexandra “Alex” Scott set up a lemonade stand to raise money for research into childhood cancers like hers. After she passed away in 2004, her parents established a foundation that has since raised more than $300 million for cancer research and funded more than 1,500 cutting-edge investigations.

Continuing its longstanding support of Dana-Farber, Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (ALSF) awarded three Institute faculty members $803,558 in grants in 2023. These will underwrite research aimed at defeating acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and rhabdomyosarcoma, an aggressive, hard-to-treat cancer of connective tissue.

The foundation extended its previous “A Award” funding to hematologic oncologist Andrew Lane, MD, PhD, who is studying the ways DNA is packed, or wound, inside blood cells. If each white blood cell’s DNA were stretched out, it would be six feet long. But in healthy cells, it is wound so tightly it will fit inside the head of a pin. One anomaly associated with AML is a protein that loosens DNA winding, and Lane’s laboratory is researching how DNA unpacking promotes leukemia and whether drugs that target DNA unpacking will kill the cancer cells.

“Projects like these will help unlock the secrets of childhood cancers.”

Liz Scott, Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation

Cancer biologist Jun Qi, PhD, received an Innovation Grant for his work to develop a new treatment for a particularly aggressive subtype of rhabdomyosarcoma, FP-RMS. Qi and his team are working on a targeted, precision medicine approach that would selectively eliminate a protein-coding gene that causes cancer cells to grow.

Susu Zhang, PhD, received a Young Investigator Award for her research into fusion-positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, one of the most difficult-to-treat childhood cancers. She is investigating the role of an enzyme called CDK8 in driving this disease, and whether attacking CDK8 could be an effective treatment.

“Projects like these will help unlock the secrets of childhood cancers,” said Liz Scott, Alex’s mother and the co-executive director of ALSF. “We cannot wait to see the results.”

excerpt.rendered: In 2000, a 4-year-old girl named Alexandra “Alex” Scott set up a lemonade stand to raise money for research into childhood cancers like hers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation continues steadfast support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The legacy of a remarkable little girl has guided the mission of Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation (ALSF) since it was established in 2005.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

title.rendered: Grant fuels pediatric brain tumor research

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Kayla Carcone

A recent $600,000 ChadTough Defeat DIPG Game Changer Grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute aims to expand treatment options for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG). This funding awarded to Robbie Majzner, MD, demonstrates dedication to advancing innovative research endeavors and Majzner’s pioneering work.

Majzner’s studies build upon his extensive experience treating children with cancer using chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells, a powerful immunotherapeutic approach. Through the foundation’s grant, he aims to test and validate a new type of CAR T cell that may be deployed to treat DIPGs with increased durability and effectiveness against these tumors, thereby offering a more potent clinical pathway.

“As parents who have experienced the devastating impact of DIPG firsthand, we are committed to supporting research that offers hope to families facing similar challenges.”

Jason Carr, ChadTough Defeat DIPG

ChadTough Defeat DIPG’s commitment to funding innovative research began with Chad Carr and Michael Mosier, the inspirations behind the organization. Chad and Michael’s courageous journeys with this devastating disease sparked a movement to accelerate research efforts and improve outcomes for other children diagnosed with DIPG. Today, Mazjner and his colleagues are focused on better understanding these tumors while elevating care standards for pediatric patients.

“As parents who have experienced the devastating impact of DIPG firsthand, we are committed to supporting research that offers hope to families facing similar challenges,” said Jason Carr, Co-Founder of ChadTough Defeat DIPG and Chad Carr’s father. “This investment in Dr. Majzner’s research represents a significant milestone in our ongoing efforts to defeat DIPG and honor of the memories of Chad and Michael.”

ChadTough Defeat DIPG’s investment stands as a testament to its unwavering commitment to advancing scientific knowledge and translating research into tangible solutions—forging a better path for patients with DIPG in Boston and around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.title: ChadTough Defeat DIPG advances research into epigenetics of pediatric brain cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The foundation's Game Changer Grant will enable concurrent genetic and epigenetic analysis to accelerate progress toward a cure.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New fellowships in pediatric brain cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The ChadTough Defeat DIPG Foundation began as two organizations founded by Jason and Tammi Carr and Mark and Jenny Mosier.

img.alt_text: Chad Tough Defeat DIPG Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Academy of Neurology Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Academy of Neurology Institute provided $150,000 to support the clinical research of Dana-Farber neurooncologist and palliative care specialist John Rhee, MD, MPH. The funds will help accelerate his work elevating care standards and developing therapeutic strategies that are better-tolerated than current options for glioma patients.

title.rendered: American Society of Hematology targets bloodborne cancers

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

For more than 60 years, the American Society of Hematology (ASH) has been funding research to improve the lives of patients with blood and bone marrow disorders. Last year, it awarded more than $550,000 in grants to seven Dana-Farber researchers seeking to understand and find new treatments for bloodborne cancers.

ASH’s 2023 grantees include Jana Ellegast, MD; Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD; David Lee, MD, MMSc, MPH; Mwanasha Merrill, MD; Oreofe Odejide, MD, MPH; Amy Wang, BA; and Becky Zon, MD.

Among the funded research is Odejide’s investigation into whether a hospice program that provides home-based palliative transfusions will make it more likely for patients with blood cancers to choose hospice, improve their end-of-life care, and reduce the need for expensive, high-intensity medical interventions.

“Right now, only about 25% of people with blood cancers enroll in hospice, and most of them do so only in the last three days of life,” she said. “We know that lack of access to transfusions—which alleviate fatigue, shortness of breath, and bleeding—is the primary reason, so we have partnered with a leading hospice organization to deliver a model of care that combines the core elements of hospice along with home transfusions.”

“ASH recognizes the remarkable contributions of these talented investigators.”

Mohandas Narla, DSc, American Society of Hematology

Zon, a fourth-year fellow, is studying why patients with hematologic malignancies have an increased risk of blood clots, which can be fatal. For unknown reasons, the danger is even more pronounced in patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs (IMiDs), a critical part of the treatment regimen for multiple myeloma. Zon is investigating the mechanisms that cause IMiD-mediated blood clots, with the goal of improving appropriate, targeted care. 

“ASH recognizes the remarkable contributions of these talented investigators,” said Mohandas Narla, DSc, ASH president and distinguished scientist at New York Blood Center Enterprises. We are proud to support them and excited to see how they improve the lives of patients living with blood disorders.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation takes aim at blood disorders
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation has awarded $1.65 million in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers studying a group of conditions caused by malfunctioning bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Celebration for the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan

title.rendered: Young patient inspires gift from stranger

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Bob Ripley reads every issue of Impact cover to cover. While reading the Late Fall 2021 edition, he was very moved by one story in particular.

In early 2020, the family of a 20-year-old woman who passed away from cancer established the Caroline Fund at Dana-Farber in her honor. The fund, which fuels research into a rare and aggressive sarcoma that Caroline had, has drawn support from countless friends and loved ones over the years.

“All I could think about was how young she was,” said Ripley. “This individual missed out on 40 years of a career and a family, and not only that but her mom and dad and siblings have missed out on those milestones, too.”

Philanthropy has always been important to Ripley, and when he comes across a program or an initiative that could have a big impact on people’s lives, he steps up. He is especially passionate about causes that support young people. Though he and Caroline never met, through a provision in his estate plans, Ripley is pledging $500,000 to support the Caroline Fund.

“I have an opportunity to help people—why wouldn’t I want to do that?”

Bob Ripley

“I have an opportunity to help people—why wouldn’t I want to do that?” he said. “Sometimes, I wish I had more resources, and then I’d be able to do even more.”

Research into rare cancers is a key priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign, and philanthropic dollars are critical to move the needle. Investments like Ripley’s help ensure that scientists will have the funding they need to pursue bold ideas—especially important for cancers that currently have limited treatment options.

“A lot of times people look at an organization and say ‘it has plenty of money, it doesn’t need any more,’ but take a look at Dana-Farber and see the many different types of cancers they’re working on,” said Ripley. “There is still so much to do. That’s really my catalyst for giving.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift to ovarian cancer inspired by story of research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In early 2022, Dr. Jean Kasmer read a story in Impact about an ovarian cancer survivor who gave to support the research of Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that…

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of Dara Frigoletto DeFeo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Feenys invest in new treatments for advanced prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In his 12 years as a prostate cancer patient, Chuck Feeny has learned quite a lot about the disease and how to navigate it. He takes each day in stride, every setback, every bit of good news and bad.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Husband honors late wife with gift to support older breast cancer patients
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the last essay she would write for her college reunion book, Virginia Aisner quoted one of her favorite lines from Vergil’s Aeneid: “Perhaps, at some time, we shall be glad to remember even these things.”

img.alt_text: A closeup shot of Virginia Aisner

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber team defies cancer in ASICS Falmouth Road Race
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Aug. 21, more than 330 members of Dana-Farber’s team ran seven miles along the scenic Cape Cod coastline for the 50th running of the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race Team Power runners

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

title.rendered: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Alison Krawczyk
Photography by Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation

Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry. When she was diagnosed with cancer in 1997, Beal turned this same commitment toward overcoming the disease. For nearly 10 years, Beal received exceptional care from Jeffrey S. Wisch, MD, who was a senior physician at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. They developed a relationship based on trust and compassion, and Beal credited Wisch with maximizing her quality of life during her treatment.

Today, the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation continues Beal’s legacy through its longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. With its most recent gift of $525,000, the foundation further supports the previously established Ilene Beal & Jeffrey S. Wisch, MD, Clinical Investigator Fund and Jeffrey S. Wisch, MD, Clinical Investigator Endowment at Dana-Farber. The fund is managed under the direction of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, director of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center and the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer.

“I am honored to continue the legacy of Ilene and Dr. Wisch.”

Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH

“I am honored to continue the legacy of Ilene and Dr. Wisch,” said Wolpin. “By channeling their generous spirits, the team and I are emboldened to continue our critical work improving outcomes for patients and their families who face gastrointestinal cancer.”

These funds support research that is integral to the mission of Dana-Farber at large, and particularly the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center, as they support the talented physicians working to identify new treatments for patients with gastrointestinal cancer.

The endowment enables the work of Dana-Farber physicians who are focused on patient-centered research, which is essential to understanding and establishing the safety and effectiveness of new treatments and to guide physicians to prescribe the right drug, for the right patient, at the right time.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Two longstanding supporters receive the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2024 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to The Herb Chambers Companies and Team Beans at a special Fenway Park ceremony.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dismantling gender disparity through mentorship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In a moment where there is so much at stake in cancer research, the Helen Gurley Brown Presidential Initiative at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is playing a critical role in dismantling this gender gap and harnessing the power and potential of women in science.

img.alt_text: Helen Gurley Brown in her office

jetpack-related-posts.title: Khannas’ generous gift helps breast cancer patients navigate care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Homai Khanna and her family are improving access to Dana-Farber's high-quality care with generous support for the Patient Navigator Program.

img.alt_text: A person wearing a mask and pointing to words on a sign

title.rendered: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Michael Quinn
Photography by Sam Ogden

Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

Recently the couple made a gift of $500,000 to advance cancer vaccine research led by Patrick Ott, MD, PhD, clinical director of the Melanoma Center and clinical science director of the Center for Immuno-Oncology at Dana-Farber. This latest gift brings their cumulative giving to an incredible $1 million.

The Kittredges’ first major gift to Dana-Farber accelerated the NeoVax clinical trial led by Ott that provided the first proof-of-concept for personalized vaccines in treating melanoma. The trial was so successful that the immune response kindled by the vaccine in participants remained robust and effective against melanoma four years later and counting, per Ott’s follow-up study. The Kittredges’ support played such an integral role in this landmark achievement that they were acknowledged by Dr. Ott in the study paper published in Nature Medicine.

“It is a privilege to support Dr. Ott’s outstanding work and we know it will continue to improve the lives of patients everywhere.”

Francis Kittredge, MD, JD

Now, with their new gift, the Kittredges are enabling Ott to pursue novel trials of melanoma vaccines in combination with other agents to enhance their efficacy and benefit more patients. According to Ott, the Kittredges’ generosity was instrumental in bringing his work this far and remains pivotal to further progress, saying, “Dr. and Mrs. Kittredge have been wonderful partners, and the lives extended by the research they support attest to their indelible impact.”  

As strong supporters of Ott’s, Dr. and Mrs. Kittredge are pleased that their philanthropy is fueling advances against melanoma while also unlocking promising new treatments for other diseases like brain cancer. He said: “It is a privilege to support Dr. Ott’s outstanding work and we know it will continue to improve the lives of patients everywhere.”

title.rendered: Garrett Whitlock named Jimmy Fund Captain

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

For the second season in a row, Boston Red Sox pitcher Garrett Whitlock is serving as Jimmy Fund Captain. In this role, he acts as an ambassador for the Jimmy Fund, building awareness and support for Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer. The Red Sox have partnered with the Jimmy Fund since 1953, the most unique and longstanding partnership in professional sports, and as Jimmy Fund Captain, Whitlock will continue this valued tradition.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024

Dear Friends,

With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic fundraising effort that will forever change cancer research and care. Since its start in 2017, The Dana-Farber Campaign has inspired more people than ever before to join our Dana-Farber and Jimmy Fund community—expanding our network of support across the country and around the world. In fact, our campaign has inspired more than 2.1 million gifts from more than 890,000 donors, with 1.4 million gifts below $100 and more than 470,000 gifts from outside New England—including all 50 states.

This progress is remarkable, and there is now enormous potential to achieve exponential success by building on our momentum. As cancer cases continue to rise at an alarming rate in the U.S., Dana-Farber must continue to diagnose cancers early, advance treatment options, and expand access to care. Fortunately, there are countless ways to be a part of The Dana-Farber Campaign and accelerate lifesaving progress.

Next-generation cancer drugs, early detection and interception, and cancer care equity are just a few examples of campaign priorities that accelerate breakthroughs for patients today and generations to come. We look to you, our valued community, to join us now and support our efforts to defy cancer, together. Visit DefyCancer.org to learn more and make a gift today.

With gratitude,

Michael Eisenson
Chair, The Dana-Farber Campaign
Trustee, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
Founding Partner and Managing Director,
Charlesbank Capital Partners

Monica Chandra
Vice Chair, The Dana-Farber Campaign
Trustee, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
President, 3EDGE Asset Management

content.rendered:
Summer 2024

Dear Friends,

Over the past seven years, The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled incredible progress at the Institute, the effects of which ripple out to help patients around the world. Our success thus far is thanks to you, our generous community members, who continue to show up and empower Dana-Farber to make breakthroughs that change cancer medicine forever.

As just one example, The Dana-Farber Campaign continues to be a catalyst for gifts that support our exceptional expertise. Our donors have established 20 new endowed chairs during the campaign, providing support for leaders across priority areas including cancer prevention, cancer care equity, nursing, and psychosocial oncology. Endowed positions like these ensure steady, permanent funding for our staff so that they can focus their time and energy where it is needed most: making the next great discovery.

While we celebrate our progress, at the same time our community mourns the loss of our dear friend and champion Larry Lucchino, who passed away in April. Words can’t express all that Larry did for Dana-Farber and all that he meant to the Jimmy Fund family. As an Institute Trustee, Chairman of the Jimmy Fund, member of The Dana-Farber Campaign Cabinet, and steadfast leader in our community, Larry set an example for all of us through his passion for our work and compassion for our patients. Dana-Farber is a special place because of people like Larry.

In times like these, we hold our community close. As we look to the future in these final months of our campaign and beyond, I hope you know how integral you are to our mission and our ability to keep changing the lives of patients everywhere.

Sincerely,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me.

jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website!

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Because of your support for The Dana-Farber Campaign, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Leon and Leslie Asadoorian gave $100,000 to advance gastrointestinal cancer research under the direction of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. Their support will help expand Wolpin’s team of clinical trial experts, enabling them to increase patient enrollment and refine and discover new treatment strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Julie Wallace Bennett
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $250,000 gift, Julie Wallace Bennett established the Peter Warren Fund for Pancreatic Research, in honor of her partner, Peter. Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber will lead this research.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of a body water

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Potential of AI and machine learning in cancer care inspires Clarks
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Steve and Joan Clark made their initial investment in artificial intelligence research in 2017, driven by a deep-seated conviction that this technology would revolutionize the world, particularly in the realm of health care and cancer care. And Dana-Farber agrees.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Promises for Purple
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2010, shortly after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and with encouragement from her two sons, Claire Muollo organized the first Promises for Purple Pancreatic Cancer Awareness 5K Walk in Braintree, Mass.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Bachrach

Ruth (pictured) and Shelly Bramson made a generous gift of more than $100,000 to support the work of Jacob Sands, MD, a physician in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. This gift is enabling Sands and his team to continue developing and improving personalized therapeutic approaches for patients with thoracic cancer.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Brendan Monahan

Sergio and Magda Brosio gave $100,000 to support the Center for Esophageal and Gastric Cancer’s biobank, with the hope that their gift inspires others. Motivated by their gratitude for Sergio’s physicians—Robert J. Mayer, MD; Scott J. Swanson, MD; and Harvey Mamon, MD, PhD—their philanthropy will expand tissue sample collection, which fuels clinical trials and other critical research to improve patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Smith Family support inspires others to help speed multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Paul Richardson has found an important partner in Robert and Dana Smith, who recently made a $3 million gift to continue supporting his advanced MM clinical trials research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phillips Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: George Phillips, together with his daughters, Kimberly and Jill, established the Juliana M. Phillips Fund Accelerating Cancer Research in honor of his late wife, Juliana, with a $150,000 gift. The fund will offer essential financial support for research into pancreatic, esophageal, gastric, and other gastrointestinal cancers, under the leadership of…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gastric Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Gastric Cancer Foundation gave $100,000 to support the research of Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, who is investigating treatments for gastric cancers with homologous recombination (HR) deficiencies that have proven effective in other types of HR-deficient cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian gave $100,000 to advance gastrointestinal cancer research under the direction of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. Their support will help expand Wolpin’s team of clinical trial experts, enabling them to increase patient enrollment and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Micki and Steven Hirsch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Clinical trials are considered essential for groundbreaking research. To help advance Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s clinical trials, Micki and Steven Hirsch made a gift of $100,000 to the Hirsch Family Fund for the Office of Clinical Research. Jeffrey Meyerhardt, MD, MPH, FASCO, leads the program which has benefited from the generous…

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Casey Reis
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Christine A. Brown Research Fellowship Fund at Dana-Farber was recently established with a $160,000 gift from Christine Brown. The fund will benefit the Department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, allowing investigators to conduct studies that seek to improve quality of life at every stage of a patient’s cancer experience.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leadership gift establishes Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care and launches health equity initiative
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber is committed to providing the best possible care to patients from all walks of life. In recent years, the Institute has prioritized expanding its clinical facilities into surrounding communities to better reach medically underserved patients with the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care model, which includes supportive services from the…

img.alt_text: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel G. Jaffe

jetpack-related-posts.title: Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at…

jetpack-related-posts.title: William Randolph Hearst Foundations
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The William Randolph Hearst Foundations gave $200,000 to fund two one-year Nurse Practitioner Adult Palliative Care Fellowships at Dana-Farber, to support two nurse practitioners in the Department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, where the focus on treating the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—helps provide patients with relief from the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dakolias gift establishes innovative collaboration in oncology nursing education
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a generous gift of $1 million, Dean and Monique Dakolias established the Dakolias Family and Lavine Family Fund for Career Development in Nursing to support educational nursing initiatives in collaboration with Northeastern University.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

The Charlie Landers Foundation awarded more than $130,000 to Dana-Farber to fund research into the development of a liquid biopsy that identifies circulating tumor DNA in patients with Ewing sarcoma, a type of cancer that forms in bone or soft tissue. If successful, this research could enable individualized treatments for patients who currently have limited options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift from Haroun Family drives critical research for adult patients with Ewing sarcoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rob Haroun and his wife, Julie, established the Haroun Family Fund with a generous gift of $1 million. Under the leadership of Suzanne George, MD, chief of the Division of Sarcoma, the fund will support innovative research aimed at discovering the next breakthroughs in treating Ewing sarcoma in adults.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Cancer Research Foundation has awarded a $200,000 research grant to Brian Crompton, MD, for his work to test a prognostic liquid biopsy approach for pediatric Ewing sarcoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Donahues drive research into liquid biopsy for early detection and personalized medicine
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Recently, Digger and Susan made a generous gift of $1 million to the Donahue Family Fund for Prostate Cancer and the Donahue Family Fund for Cancer Interception at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop establishes Therapeutic Food Pantry
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: To help combat food insecurity among cancer patients, Stop & Shop made a $1 million gift to establish the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Therapeutic Food Pantry, an equity-driven, cross-sector partnership to eliminate barriers that disrupt access to food and impact social determinants of health.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Janower family drives pediatric brain tumor research forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cindy and AJ Janower’s introduction to the challenging world of childhood cancer began when their daughter, Samantha “Sammi,” was just three years old.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One Mission
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One Mission recently demonstrated its commitment to cancer patients with two gifts totaling nearly $220,000 in support of the Blum Pediatric Resource Room and Pediatric Resource Program at Dana-Farber. One Mission, founded in 2008 by Ashley and Ari Haseotes, aims to help families cope with the emotional and financial challenges…

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Oifer and Linda Zarchin
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $150,000 gift from David Oifer and Linda Zarchin will expand support for Dana-Farber’s Matilda Rose Danoff Fund for Pediatric Spinal Cord Tumor Research. content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict drug resistance and detect cancer earlier.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Casey Reis

The Michael Coughlin Lung Cancer Research Fund, established in memory of Michael Coughlin, recently surpassed $100,000 in funds generated in support of thoracic oncology at Dana-Farber. The majority of these funds were raised through the family’s Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk team, Coughlin Crew, which first participated in the event in 2018.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

img.alt_text: Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk defies cancer with $9.4 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to more than 8,400 participants, the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk surpassed $185 million in funds raised over 37 years for Dana-Farber's lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo, with one person holding a framed t-shirt with signatures

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Josh Campbell

Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.
