jetpack-related-posts.title: John Cassidy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Cassidy’s generous $300,000 gift establishes the Cassidy Family Melanoma Fellowship, to significantly advance melanoma research. Under the guidance of principal investigator F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber, this funding will help support the mentorship of an early career investigator, fostering innovation…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

img.alt_text: Lena Maximo Robinson and Richard Robinson.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Martin family’s events surpass $1 million milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber celebrated the more than $1 million cumulatively raised by the family of the late Sharon Crowley Martin through events including Derby Day, a Kentucky Derby-themed cocktail watch party.

img.alt_text: The Martin family receiving an award

jetpack-related-posts.title: Derby Day
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Siblings Susie Mitchell, Lisa Fideli, and Chuck Martin once again hosted their Derby Day fundraiser in memory of their mother, Sharon Crowley Martin, who passed away from melanoma in 2007. They raised $143,000 to advance the vital research of Dana-Farber’s Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma, F. Stephen Hodi Jr.,…

img.alt_text: A crowd of people inside a tent with colorful globe lights

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crowley gift accelerates innovative research in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley are longtime supporters of Dana-Farber who made their first gift nearly two decades ago to advance melanoma research in memory of Brian’s sister.

By Brendan Monahan

Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards over $1.1 million to Dana-Farber for WM research advancements
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has taken a significant step forward in combating Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM) by awarding four Dana-Farber scientists more than $1.1 million in grants. This generous funding is intended to fuel groundbreaking studies that aim to uncover the mechanisms behind WM development, pinpoint vulnerabilities, and identify…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Bayer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Furthering research into new treatment for Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: More than 10 years ago, Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and his colleagues were the first scientists to discover that MYD88 mutations, which occur in more than 95% of patients with Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM), rely on the BTK protein to function.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fred and Michele Brettschneider
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato made a gift of $100,000 to support research within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia at Dana-Farber. The center is the largest in the world dedicated to the study of Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a slow-growing type of blood cancer that most often forms in the bone marrow.

CURE Childhood Cancer awarded $330,000 to support research led by Yana Pikman, MD, as she tests a new combination therapy for leukemia with RAS signaling pathway mutations. jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

Irene fulfilled Paul Derocher’s wishes by giving $100,000 to establish the Paul Derocher Fund for Small Intestine Cancer Research. Derocher’s support is enabling Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, to continue his research into better early detection and treatment strategies for small intestine cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Gastric Cancer Foundation gave $100,000 to support the research of Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, who is investigating treatments for gastric cancers with homologous recombination (HR) deficiencies that have proven effective in other types of HR-deficient cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact

title.rendered: Oliver S. and Jennie R. Donaldson Charitable Trust

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Bethany Herrema
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Donaldson Charitable Trust gave nearly $195,000 to support the PROMISE study led by Irene Ghobrial, MD. This nationwide study aims to better understand the higher rates of a multiple myeloma precursor condition in older adults who are Black or who have a close family member with blood cancer.

Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Paving the way to cancer prevention
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Wycliffe “Wyc” Grousbeck and Emilia Fazzalari are firm believers that “good things don’t come easy.” As philanthropic and entrepreneurial leaders in the Boston community, they seek out innovative and exceptional people who are tackling groundbreaking endeavors that are simply too compelling to refuse.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Brendan Monahan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Dale Fishman gave $243,000 to fuel pioneering research led by Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD; Catherine Wu, MD; and physician-scientists across Dana-Farber. Fishman’s multifaceted philanthropy is empowering these investigators to advance novel cellular therapies for pancreatic cancer and personalized cancer vaccines, while bolstering the Faculty Research Fund, which together pave the way for new lifesaving treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: The promise of personalized cancer vaccines
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds raised through The Dana-Farber campaign are expanding the benefits of personalized cancer vaccines pioneered here.

img.alt_text: Two scientists examining a slide in a lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pancreatic Cancer Action Network
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon invests in promising early career scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $3.2 million in grants to nine early career investigators at Dana-Farber, including Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, who was named the foundation’s first Damon Runyon-David M. Livingston, MD, Physician-Scientist.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Casey Reis

The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. Investment from the Maine-based non-profit will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

Summer 2024
By Robbie Merritt
Photography by Josh Campbell

With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

content.rendered:
Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan

The Human Frontier Science Program, an organization that promotes international collaboration in basic research, awarded grants totaling more than $400,000 to fund biochemistry research at Dana-Farber. The funding supports two early career researchers pursuing projects that seek to deepen our understanding of the tumor microenvironment and develop cutting-edge strategies to harness the immune system against cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: BTC has awarded $22.9 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers working across multiple institutions to unlock the secrets of four difficult-to-treat cancers and intercept or develop cutting-edge treatments for them.

Summer 2024
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Dienna and John Lehner recommended a gift totaling $100,000 to the board of the Orchard Foundation, to support leukemia research under the direction of Dana-Farber researchers, Robert Soiffer, MD, and Daniel DeAngelo, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kesslers expedite research to expand treatment options for AML
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A crucial infusion of funds from Michele and Howard Kessler is enabling the clinical trial of a promising combination treatment.

img.alt_text: A couple poses for a photo in front of a flower display

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: October Saves
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Hockey goalies across the nation raised $100,000 for Dana-Farber through October Saves by gathering pledges for each save during Breast Cancer Awareness Month. These funds support the pediatric leukemia research of Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD (pictured far left), and Wallace Bourgeois, MD (second from left), in honor of Charlie Capalbo,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: 3000 Miles to a Cure
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: 3000 Miles to a Cure awarded $100,000 to support the ALLELE-GBM research program at Dana-Farber, under the direction of Keith Ligon, MD, PhD. Ligon’s team is working to put genomic data into the hands of patients, providers, and researchers to advance treatments and clinical trials in glioblastoma (GBM).
